newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Small players boost Nigerian share trade.
newsitem.headline: Small players boost Nigerian share trade.

text.p: Nigerian shares closed a notch higher on Wednesday on gains by small firms, traders said.
The index edged up to 8518.61 from Tuesday's 8517.46, the third consecutive rise.
"Not much activity was recorded among the blue chips today," one trader said.

Most leading stocks were unchanged because investors were not keen on them, dealers said. But food company Nestle gained 10 kobo to 48.80 naira and oil miller P.S. Mandrides rose five kobo to 5.95 naira.
International Merchant Bank added four kobo to 1.41 naira, while Wema Bank finished five up at 3.30 naira. First Bank, the sectoral leader fell 12 kobo to 14.36 naira.
B.O.C. Gases, formerly Industrial Gases was up seven kobo at 14.87 naira and Carnaud Metal Box rose one kobo to 2.96 naira.
Construction firms Cappa and D'Alberto were up five kobo each at 12.15 naira and Roads rose 1.30 naira, up one kobo.
Investors selling Cadbury caused it to closing 10 kobo lower at 36.10 naira. Unipetrol fell five kobo to 68.15 naira, while Ashaka Cement fell two kobo to 12.98 naira.
